why: Science covers physics chemistry maths and biology — the widest range of career options after 12th.
note: Day-to-day in 11th-12th: solving problems lab work and heavy theory. Opens the most doors after 12th.
next_step_1: Look at the actual 11th syllabus for PCM and PCB — pick based on which subjects you enjoy not career outcomes
next_step_2: Talk to someone in 11th Science and ask what the workload is actually like
next_step_3: Decide between PCM (engineering path) and PCB (medical path) before the school year starts

why: Commerce covers business economics and accounting — leads to CA MBA banking and management roles.
note: Day-to-day in 11th-12th: numbers business concepts and case studies. Leads to finance and management careers.
next_step_1: Look at what Accountancy and Business Studies cover in 11th — it's different from what most people expect
next_step_2: Talk to a CA student or commerce graduate about what the first year actually involves
next_step_3: Decide early whether you want Maths in commerce — it opens more options but adds difficulty

why: Arts covers history psychology political science and literature — the most flexible stream for law civil services and media.
note: Day-to-day in 11th-12th: reading writing and analysis. Best path for law civil services and media.
next_step_1: Pick 2-3 subjects from the arts stream that genuinely interest you and read one chapter from each
next_step_2: Look at what careers arts leads to — law civil services journalism psychology are all real options
next_step_3: Talk to someone in 11th Arts about what the workload and subject depth is like

why: Vocational gives you a practical skill alongside academics — you can start working sooner than most streams.
note: Day-to-day in 11th-12th: practical skill training alongside basic academics. Fastest path to employment.
next_step_1: Research which vocational trade has the best job market in your city right now
next_step_2: Check if your target colleges accept vocational stream students for lateral entry programs
next_step_3: Talk to someone working in your chosen trade about what skills actually get people hired

why: Sports stream lets you train seriously while completing 11th and 12th — the right path if you're competing at a serious level.
note: Day-to-day in 11th-12th: structured training plus academics. Right path only if you're competing seriously.
next_step_1: Get an honest assessment from your coach about your competitive level — not encouragement a real evaluation
next_step_2: Check which schools in your area have strong sports programs and what they offer academically
next_step_3: Have a backup plan — sports science or coaching is a real career if professional sports doesn't work out

why: Fine Arts covers drawing design and performance — leads to animation UX film and creative industries.
note: Day-to-day in 11th-12th: studio work portfolio building and creative projects. Leads to design and media careers.
next_step_1: Start building a portfolio now — even rough work. The earlier you start the better your options at 12th
next_step_2: Look at what animation UX design and graphic design careers actually involve day-to-day
next_step_3: Check which colleges have strong fine arts or design programs and what their entry requirements are

why: Agriculture covers farming soil science and food systems — increasingly relevant with agritech and food startups.
note: Day-to-day in 11th-12th: field work biology and chemistry. Growing demand in agritech and food systems.
next_step_1: Visit one agritech startup or agricultural college to see what modern agriculture actually looks like
next_step_2: Check the 11th Agriculture syllabus — it's more science-heavy than most people expect
next_step_3: Look at agritech and food science careers alongside traditional agriculture roles
